llm.summary: The skill has a coherent document-generation purpose, but its setup guide tells users to permanently weaken Figma HTTPS protections while handling Figma tokens and design data.

dimensions.detail: Local indexing and output files are proportionate to the workflow, but Figma token use plus disabled TLS/proxy handling is disproportionate for document generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is mostly normal, but the manual instructs users to modify the separate Figma skill to disable TLS certificate verification and suppress warnings; it also suggests unpinned pip installs in troubleshooting.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill directs recursive indexing of a configured historical-project root and later reading matched documents; this is purpose-aligned but broadly scoped and not paired with clear consent, exclusion, or least-privilege guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background service or privilege escalation was found, but the guide recommends a persistent source-code change to the Figma client that leaves authenticated Figma traffic less protected across future runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Generating proposals from historical project folders and Figma files matches the stated purpose, but those inputs can contain sensitive business/design data and the documentation lacks strong privacy boundaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Use only approved historical-project folders, avoid secrets or regulated data, and do not follow the manual's instruction to set verify=False or suppress HTTPS warnings for Figma. If using Figma, keep the token read-only, store it securely, and use proper trusted CA/proxy configuration instead of disabling certificate checks.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: the manual instructs adding urllib3 warning suppression and setting requests session verify=False for Figma API use; this is unsafe and not required for the stated document-generation purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the Figma troubleshooting section tells users to bypass proxy/TLS certificate validation, which can expose tokens and design data to interception.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly confirmed: reading historical project files and Figma designs is expected for this skill, but the artifacts under-disclose confidentiality and safe-handling expectations; the TLS-bypass guidance is not expected.
[T08] unexpected: Confirmed but lower-weight: the manual suggests pip install requests python-docx without pinning or hashes, while the included scripts themselves use only the standard library.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: repository validation, file counting, indexing, and upload-precheck utilities are disclosed maintenance/developer functions, not hidden tool poisoning.
[P2] unexpected: Downgraded: inspected files contain UTF-8 BOMs and stray control characters around malformed code-fence labels, but no hidden role-change, exfiltration, or override instructions were found.
[TM1] expected: Downgraded: rm data/project_index.json is a documented manual cleanup of the generated index file, not a broad destructive command.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded in part: Figma access-token setup is expected for optional Figma integration and recommends read-only scope, but token handling becomes risky when combined with the TLS-bypass instructions.
[LP3] expected: Partly confirmed: filesystem reads and index writes are central to the skill, but explicit permission boundaries and exclusion guidance are missing.
[SQP-3] expected: Not treated as a security blocker: the artifacts are primarily Chinese-language and future multilingual support is mentioned, but this does not indicate malicious behavior.
